You have harmed me greatly (by making the statement). May Allaah not forgive you." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "He is right. By Allaah! neither has he caused any rift nor has he perpetrated any of the other wrongs. Do forgive me for that." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then continued pleading with the man (to forgive him) until he eventually did. [^1]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) Seeks Pardon from Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA)

Hadhrat Rajaa bin Rabee'ah narrates that he was once sitting in the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ in Madinah. In the gathering with him were the likes of Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA). When Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) passed by and greeted them with Salaam, they all replied with the exception of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA), who remained silent. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) then watched Hadhrat Hasan (RA) leave and then replied:

He then said further, "Of all the inhabitants of the earth, that man is most beloved to the inhabitants of the heavens. By Allaah! I have not spoken to him since the days of the Battle of Siffeen." Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) said, "Why do you then not go to him and present your excuse." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) agreed and when they went to Hadhrat Hasan (RA)'s house, Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) asked permission to enter. He then entered and requested permission for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) to enter.

(When they had entered) Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA), "Tell us what you just said when Hasan passed by." "Of course," replied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA), "I had told you that of all the inhabitants of the earth, this man is most beloved to the inhabitants of the heavens." Hadhrat Hasan (RA) then said, "If you knew that I am the most beloved person on earth to the inhabitants of the heavens, why did you fight us and strengthen the ranks of the others during the Battle of Siffeen?" Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) submitted, "I swear by Allaah that I neither strengthened their ranks nor wielded a sword with them. I just happened to be with my father."
